investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-08-27T14:28Z with an identical 502 bad_gateway error indicating the swarm gateway ELB endpoint at /v1/agents was unreachable during agent provisioning. investigation.rootCause: The swarm gateway — an AWS ELB in us-east-2 fronting the /v1/agents provisioning endpoint — was unreachable at the time of the eval run. The production-api layer returned HTTP 502 with code "bad_gateway" on POST /api/agents for every remote-agents check. Because the failure happens at the network/gateway boundary before the agent creation call can complete, no evidence is produced and all downstream assertions (vmIdPresent, remoteState) cannot be evaluated. This is an eval-observed infrastructure availability signal, not confirmed user-traffic impact; no incident or traffic evidence is present in the packet.

investigations.title: image-generation-stream Eval Failure: OpenAI API Credit Balance Exhausted on /api/generate/image/stream

This is an eval infrastructure failure caused by an exhausted external API billing account; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

The AURA backend propagated this as a `generation_error` SSE frame with `code: GENERATION_FAILED`, terminating the stream before any `generation_completed` frame or image artifact URL could be emitted. The eval contract at `infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json` line 343–344 requires both `generation_completed` in `frameTypes` and `imageUrlPresent: true`, neither of which was satisfied.

If the snapshot file's Last-Modified HTTP header is within the past 300 minutes but the embedded generation timestamp is stale, the cause would be a timestamp computation bug in the workflow rather than a missed run.
If sibling checks had also failed (e.g., public-observability-page returning non-200), a broader infrastructure outage would be implicated rather than a workflow scheduling failure.
followUpEvals: Add an eval that directly checks the GitHub Actions workflow run recency for the snapshot-publishing workflow, so a missed or failed run is detected independently of the snapshot age.
Add a snapshotAgeMinutes warning-threshold eval (e.g., warn at 180 minutes) to provide earlier signal before the 300-minute hard failure boundary is breached.

Add an eval that compares the snapshot's embedded generatedAt timestamp against the HTTP Last-Modified header from GitHub Pages, to detect cases where the file is served stale due to CDN caching rather than a missed workflow run.

Reconcile the staleAfterMinutes=360 value in infra/evals/status/features.json with the snapshotAgeMinutes max=300 assertion in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json and add an eval or lint check that enforces consistency between these two thresholds.
